q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution

NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 earnings release will occur in approximately late August 2026 (about 2 weeks from today, 2026-08-17). The actual guidance will be provided at that earnings call.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The most likely outcome is that NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 forward guidance will be in the range of **102-104 billion dollars**, representing approximately 12-14% sequential growth from the Q1 FY2027 guidance of $91.0 billion.

**Reasoning:**
- Q1 FY2027 guidance was $91.0B (midpoint), issued May 20, 2026
- NVIDIA has demonstrated strong sequential growth momentum in data center and AI accelerators
- Historical quarterly growth rates for NVIDIA in high-demand periods: typically 10-20% sequential growth
- The AI infrastructure boom continues with strong demand signals from hyperscalers
- No major negative catalysts mentioned in the research (China restrictions already factored into guidance)
- Conservative margin: historically NVIDIA tends to guide conservatively and beat, but the guidance mechanism is designed to be achievable

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Demand weakness**: Unexpected pullback in hyperscaler capex (though no signals of this in current environment)
- **Macro shock**: Broader tech/economic slowdown impacting AI investment
- **Supply constraints**: Inability to fulfill orders despite demand
- **Geopolitical escalation**: Additional China export restrictions beyond current assumptions
- **Inventory corrections**: Customers reducing orders after period of buildout
- **Competitive pressure**: Market share loss to AMD or other alternatives
- **Conservative guidance philosophy**: NVIDIA might guide lower to ensure achievement

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Demand acceleration**: Stronger-than-expected hyperscaler spending on new GPU generations
- **ASP expansion**: Mix shift toward higher-margin H100/H200 products
- **New customer wins**: Enterprise and cloud adoption expanding beyond hyperscalers
- **China policy reversal**: Unexpected loosening of restrictions adding incremental revenue
- **Product shortages driving pricing**: Strong supply/demand dynamics enabling higher pricing
- **Beat-and-raise pattern**: If management wants to continue momentum of positive surprises

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided:
- **Q1 FY2027 guidance: $91.0 billion** (with ±2% margin = $89.2B - $92.8B range)
- Historical sequential growth rates in AI boom periods: The fact that Q1 FY2027 was "notably above the average quarterly revenue estimate of $86.84 billion" suggests 5% outperformance to guidance vs consensus

For a company in hypergrowth with strong demand signals, typical sequential guidance increases range from 8-18%. Given NVIDIA's position and the data center tailwinds, 12% sequential growth is a reasonable base rate expectation.

---

## Probability Distribution

Given:
- Midpoint of prior guidance: $91.0B
- Expected sequential growth: 12% = $102B as central estimate
- Uncertainty band: ±6-7% around that midpoint

The range 99.5B - 115.5B represents approximately -9.4% to +26.9% variance from the $91B baseline, or -2.9% to +12.9% from my $102B central estimate.

At the **10th percentile** (conservative guidance scenario): $99.5B
At the **50th percentile** (most likely): $102.5B  
At the **90th percentile** (bullish scenario): $109.0B

Low (10th percentile): 99500000000
Median (50th percentile): 102500000000
High (90th percentile): 109000000000
q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA released its Q1 FY2027 earnings on May 20, 2026, and provided forward guidance for Q2 FY2027. The company expects revenue to be $91.0 billion, with a margin of plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027/). This figure is notably above the average quarterly revenue estimate of $86.84 billion from LSEG [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). NVIDIA explicitly stated that this outlook does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html).

Additionally, NVIDIA anticipates GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins to be 74.9% and 75.0% respectively, with a variability of plus or minus 50 basis points. GAAP and non-GAAP operating expenses are projected to be approximately $8.5 billion and $8.3 billion, respectively [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). For the full fiscal year 2027, the company expects GAAP and non-GAAP tax rates to range between 16.0% and 18.0% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm).
